chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muawiya ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Sayrafi, from one of our companions who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa: is it an Obligation or a Sunnah? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is an Obligation.'
I said: 'Is it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "there is no blame on him if he goes round them both"?'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'That was regarding the Umra of the adjudication (Umrat al-Qada).'
Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stipulated upon them that they would raise (remove) the idols from Al-Safa and Al-Marwa.
So a man pretended to be busy and neglected the Sa'ee until the days had passed, and the idols returned.
So they (people) came to him (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! So-and-so did not perform Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, and the idols have returned.'
Therefore, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed: "there is no blame on him if he goes round them both"
i.e., and upon them were the idols.

key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'ee (ritual walking between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: Is the Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa obligatory or a Sunnah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the Sa'ee as a fundamental pillar (Fard) of Hajj and Umrah, resolving the apparent contradiction with the verse 'there is no blame on him' (2:158) by contextualizing it within the Umrat al-Qada. The verse specifically addressed the temporary state where idols still occupied the hills, confirming that the ritual's validity was not contingent on the immediate removal of pagan symbols but on the act of pilgrimage itself. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that the core obligation remains intact regardless of external ritualistic conditions.
